description:
If There Are Trillions of Stars, Why Is the Night Sky Dark?

If the universe were endless and full of stars, every direction would end on a star and the night sky would blaze. It doesn't, because the universe has an age, and it is expanding.

Follow for daily trips through the universe. 🚀

segments.text: If there are trillions of stars, why is the night sky dark?

visual.query: Hubble ultra deep field high rez edit1
commons: Hubble ultra deep field high rez edit1

segments.text: Think about it. If space went on forever, filled with stars, every direction you look would end on a star.
segments.headline: Stars in every direction

segments.text: The whole sky would be as bright as the surface of the Sun. Day and night.

visual.label: a sky with no dark gaps

segments.text: This puzzle is called Olbers' paradox. The answer is hiding in the dark itself.
segments.headline: Olbers' paradox

segments.text: The universe is about thirteen point eight billion years old. Light from stars farther away hasn't had time to reach us yet.
And space is expanding, stretching old light until our eyes can't see it.
segments.headline: Stretched light

segments.text: So every time you see a dark night sky, you're seeing proof that the universe had a beginning.
